title: OCC Says 97.7% of Its Tracked Mortgages Performed, Yet Starts Rose
description: OCC's September 23 mortgage report covers about 18.8% of U.S. residential mortgage debt. It found 97.7% current and performing in Q2, while new foreclosures increased.
author: James Park
body: The OCC's second-quarter mortgage report, released September 23, says 97.7% of mortgages in its federal-banking-system sample were current and performing at quarter-end, up from 97.5% a year earlier. At the same time, servicers initiated 7,904 foreclosures during the quarter, up from both the previous quarter and a year earlier. Both statements can be true: they describe different measures and different denominators.

The agency also counted 7,349 completed loan modifications in the quarter, a 16.5% increase over the prior quarter's 6,308. Most modifications combined several changes intended to improve affordability and sustainability. The report includes about 10.1 million first-lien loans, representing roughly 18.8% of U.S. residential mortgage debt, through June 30, 2026. It is not a survey of every mortgage or a forecast of what one borrower's lender will do.

If you are struggling to pay, contact the servicer early and ask which loss-mitigation options apply to your loan. HUD lists free housing-counseling help for homeowners at risk of foreclosure. The separate ICE August delinquency figures cover a later month and a different data pool; do not compare the two percentages as if they measure the same set of mortgages.

sources.label: OCC September 23 second-quarter mortgage metrics
HUD resources for avoiding foreclosure

title: Brooklyn Rental Applicants May Get Deposits Back After Blacklisting Case
description: A September 18 New York settlement requires $150,000 in restitution for certain apartment applicants and bans the firm's use of housing-court history in screening.
author: David Chen
body: New York's attorney general says Brooklyn High Rise LLC agreed September 18 to pay $150,000 in restitution to certain apartment applicants who paid a 'good faith deposit' but withdrew or were denied housing and did not get it back. The state also imposed $202,250 in penalties for unlawful tenant blacklisting. The penalty goes to the state; it is not another pool of individual deposit refunds.

According to the office, the firm denied housing to more than 200 applicants using prior housing-court records, contrary to New York's protections. It also charged applicants $500 to $750 to hold units while processing applications, promising the money would go toward rent but failing to return some deposits. The agreement requires it to stop seeking housing-court history in screening and change its application practices.

An applicant who dealt with this firm should keep proof of the deposit, the application and any denial or withdrawal. The state release says all tenants meeting the restitution criteria will receive refunds, but it does not establish that every person ever rejected by a Brooklyn landlord gets a check. If you have a separate screening issue, check the state's guidance and document what the landlord requested; Financialist's general debt guides do not replace tenant-rights advice.

sources.label: New York Attorney General September 18 Brooklyn High Rise settlement

title: New York Orders $1 Million-Plus in DARCARS Refunds. Check Your Paperwork
description: Two Westchester DARCARS dealers must reimburse eligible buyers and lessees for sales-commission and add-on charges, says the NY attorney general's September 16 settlement.
author: David Chen
body: New York's attorney general announced September 16 that two Westchester DARCARS dealerships agreed to more than $1 million in customer refunds over sales-commission charges and an add-on bundle. The affected dealers are DARCARS Lexus of Mount Kisco and DARCARS BMW. The settlement concerns specific transactions, not every purchase from the DARCARS group.

The attorney general says DARCARS Lexus must return $892,671.26 to people charged a sales-commission fee from October 23, 2021 through May 30, 2022. Both dealers must make additional reimbursements totaling $281,847.72 connected to misleading add-on practices. The office says thousands who bought or leased cars may be eligible and the dealers must stop the described fee practices. The amounts are aggregate obligations, not an individual check estimate.

If you bought or leased at either location in the affected period, keep your signed contract, itemized sale and lease paperwork and any correspondence. Look for sales-commission fees and DARCARS Assurance charges; the state's release provides the exact dealer names and settlement terms. Do not pay an outside 'claims agent' to tell you whether the state has identified you. Ask the attorney general's office or dealership about your particular transaction, rather than assuming the settlement covers every add-on from every dealer.

sources.label: New York Attorney General September 16 DARCARS settlement

title: FleetCor's $100 Million FTC Deal Could Repay Businesses, but Not Yet
description: The FTC's September 17 proposed FleetCor/Corpay order sets aside $100 million for harmed fuel-card customers. Comment and refund mechanics are still pending.
author: James Park
body: FleetCor, now called Corpay, and its CEO agreed to pay $100 million to resolve an FTC administrative action over fuel-card fees and claimed savings, the agency announced September 17. The proposed payment would be used for redress to business customers harmed by the conduct. It is not a current application for a guaranteed payment to every small business that used a fuel card.

The FTC alleged undisclosed or unauthorized charges, late fees even when customers paid on time or could not pay on time, and misleading claims about gas savings and fraud controls. A federal district court in 2023 entered summary judgment for the FTC on its claims, the agency says, while the new administrative consent agreement still has a separate process before it is final.

The FTC expects a Federal Register notice followed by 30 days of public comment before it decides whether to make the proposed consent order final. The September 17 release does not state individual refund amounts, a claim form or payment date. A business owner can preserve statements, fee records and contracts while checking official FTC updates. Compare any fuel-card offer using total fees and actual pump-price discounts, not the advertised savings alone.

sources.label: FTC September 17 FleetCor administrative settlement proposal

title: Amway's Proposed $225 Million FTC Deal Is Not a Refund Form Yet
description: The FTC says a proposed Amway settlement would fund redress for harmed sellers and change recruitment practices. No claim instructions were announced in the September 17 release.
author: David Chen
body: The FTC and Washington state announced a proposed $225 million order September 17 involving Amway and two approved-provider groups, World Wide Group and Leadership Team Development. The agencies allege misleading earnings claims and pressure to buy products and training. Nearly all of the proposed monetary relief would be used to compensate certain harmed participants. That is not an announced check for every person who ever joined Amway.

In its complaint, the FTC alleges that most participants joining the two groups after 2020 spent more on products and training than they made from Amway. The proposed order would require stronger sales records and outside auditing, reduce certain incentives tied to recruits' purchases and bar the groups from charging new participants for training in their first year. These are allegations and proposed remedies; a stipulated final order has force only after court approval and signature.

The FTC explicitly said it would provide redress-program information later. As of that release, there was no official FTC claim form, payout date or eligibility test to complete. Anyone approached with an 'Amway refund' request for an upfront fee should verify it on the FTC's own case or refund pages before responding. Independent sellers considering any MLM should compare actual net income after inventory, travel and training costs, not only gross sales or recruitment promises.

sources.label: FTC September 17 Amway proposed-order announcement

title: Fed's Stablecoin Plan: Full Reserves Proposed, Not Yet Required by This Rule
description: The Fed's September 24 proposals would set reserves, capital and application rules for issuers it supervises. The comment window depends on Federal Register publication.
author: James Park
body: The Federal Reserve released two stablecoin proposals September 24 under the GENIUS Act. One would require payment-stablecoin issuers supervised by the Board to fully back their coins with eligible reserve assets, including certain short-term Treasury bills and other liquid assets. It would also set standardized capital and risk-management standards. Those are proposals, not a declaration that a buyer's particular stablecoin already satisfies them.

A separate proposal would set an application process for Board-supervised banks seeking approval to issue payment stablecoins. Applicants would submit a business plan and financial information, with procedures for appeals and decisions. The Fed also proposes rules for supervised firms safeguarding reserve assets and clarification of bank stablecoin activities.

The Fed says comments close 60 days after publication in the Federal Register, rather than giving a fixed date in its September 24 release. A stablecoin holder should check who issues the token, what claims the holder has against that issuer and the current reserve disclosures. Do not treat a proposed federal framework as deposit insurance, an investment return or a guarantee that one token can always be redeemed at par.

sources.label: Federal Reserve September 24 stablecoin proposals

title: FTC's Corteva Deal Targets Pesticide Prices, Not Immediate Farmer Refunds
description: A September 28 proposed FTC-Corteva order would end certain distributor loyalty terms for 10 years. Farmers may gain generic choices, but no personal refund was announced.
author: David Chen
body: The Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general announced a September 28 proposed settlement with Corteva over pesticide-distributor loyalty terms. The FTC says the program deterred distributors from carrying generic competitors after pesticide patents expired. The agreement would restrict those practices for 10 years, potentially making lower-priced products easier for farmers to buy. That is a competition remedy, not a price guarantee at the next farm-supply purchase.

The FTC's 2022 lawsuit alleges that distributors received end-of-year incentives for buying nearly all of certain pesticide ingredients from Corteva, excluding lower-priced competitors. Under the proposed order, Corteva could not condition distributor benefits on buying more than 50% of a given active ingredient from it or restrict generic purchases to under 50%. The order would extend across Corteva's post-patent active ingredients, not only the examples in the lawsuit.

The commission said the Corteva agreement resolves only its claims against that company; litigation against Syngenta continues. The proposed order was filed in federal court and would become enforceable upon court approval. The release mentions money to state plaintiffs, but does not announce an individual farmer-refund or claim process. Farmers comparing pesticide offers should ask distributors for equivalent active ingredients, product labels and current prices rather than assuming the lawsuit has already lowered every price.

sources.label: FTC and states, September 28 proposed Corteva settlement

title: Mortgage Delinquencies Hit 3.53% in August. The Headline Needs Context
description: ICE's September 28 first look says August mortgage delinquency rose to 3.53%, partly a calendar effect, while serious late payments rose year over year.
author: James Park
body: ICE Mortgage Technology's September 28 first look puts the August 2026 national mortgage delinquency rate at 3.53%, up 0.14 percentage point from July. The company says this rise was effectively flat after a calendar-driven decline the month before. A one-month move alone is not evidence of a sudden foreclosure wave.

The more concerning measure is serious delinquency: ICE estimates 574,000 loans were seriously delinquent at the end of August, up 11,000 for the month and 19% from a year earlier. It puts that share at 1.04% of active loans. Foreclosure starts fell 6% in August but remained 29% above a year earlier. Pre-sale foreclosure inventory was 0.54% of active loans, unchanged for the month but up by 89,000 loans, or 41%, over the year.

These are ICE estimates extrapolated from its loan-level mortgage database, not a census of every borrower. Its release says whole-number loan counts are generally rounded. A borrower behind on payments should contact their servicer before ignoring a notice and can seek a HUD-approved housing counselor; the data does not determine anyone's eligibility for help. The separate OCC and FHFA second-quarter reports cover different loan populations and time windows, so their percentages are not interchangeable with ICE's August figure.

sources.label: ICE Mortgage Technology, August first look published September 28
HUD avoiding foreclosure resources

title: Selling Farmland? IRS Proposes How Four-Year Tax Payments Would Work
description: The IRS released proposed rules September 28 for qualifying farmland sellers to pay tax on gain over four annual installments. The proposal is not a general tax extension.
author: James Park
body: The IRS and Treasury issued proposed regulations September 28 on a narrow tax election for qualifying sales or exchanges of farmland to an individual actively engaged in farming. Section 1062 allows an eligible seller to pay the tax attributable to the gain in four equal annual installments, rather than all at once. That does not mean the entire sale price is tax-free or that every land sale qualifies.

According to the IRS release, eligible U.S. real property generally must have been used for farming, or leased to a qualified farmer, during substantially all of the preceding 10 years. A legally enforceable restriction must generally keep the property in farming for 10 years after sale. The buyer must be an individual actively farming. Qualifying transactions are in taxable years beginning after July 4, 2025.

The proposal says each installment would be 25% of the applicable tax liability. The first would generally be due by the regular return due date for the sale year without regard to extensions; later installments would be due on following years' regular return due dates. Proposed rules also explain pass-through entities and temporary gaps in farming use. The IRS is taking comments through November 30, 2026. A seller considering this election should review current statute, the proposal and their specific facts with a tax professional before closing.

sources.label: IRS September 28 proposed-regulation announcement

title: O'Reilly Text Settlement Claims Close Today: Who May Get Up to $22
description: A proposed O'Reilly Automotive text-message settlement has a September 28 claim deadline. Eligibility is narrow, payment is not guaranteed, and court approval remains pending.
author: David Chen
body: A proposed settlement over O'Reilly Automotive marketing texts has a claim deadline today, September 28, 2026. The case concerns people who received two or more texts after their number was assigned to them while it was on the National Do Not Call Registry. A person with a qualifying claim may receive up to $22, but the amount may be reduced if claims exceed the fund. This is not a payment to every O'Reilly customer.

The settlement site's notice says a claimant's application may be denied if they made an online or in-store O'Reilly purchase during the 18 months before the texts. O'Reilly denies wrongdoing, and a court has not ruled on the merits. The court must still approve the settlement before payment; the claims deadline is not the payment date.

The site says online claims must be submitted September 28, or paper claims postmarked by that date. The same page lists a separate objection deadline of October 6. Before sharing personal information, check the court case number, Bryan v. O'Reilly Automotive, Inc., No. 2026CH000016, and check the settlement administrator site linked in the court notice yourself. Financialist has not authenticated any individual unsolicited settlement message; do not treat a text asking for a fee or bank password as proof you qualify.

sources.label: Settlement administrator's case notice and deadlines, checked September 28
LaSalle County preliminary approval order, e-filed June 29, hosted by ClassAction.org

title: Florida Clears Four Home Insurance Rate Cuts. Will Your Renewal Be Cheaper?
description: Florida says four approved insurer rate decreases affect more than 62,000 policies. The cuts take effect at renewal and do not guarantee a lower bill for every homeowner.
author: James Park
body: Florida's insurance regulator says it approved four homeowners-insurance rate decreases affecting more than 62,000 policies. For those covered by the four insurers, the changes take effect at renewal. A statewide headline does not mean every homeowner gets a cut, or that an individual renewal bill will fall by the same percentage.

In its September 22 announcement, the Office of Insurance Regulation identified One Alliance North America Insurance Company, Safe Harbor Insurance Company, Unique Insurance Company and Vyrd Insurance Company. The office listed decreases of 10.4%, 4.1%, 3.2% and 10.4%, respectively, affecting 17,148, 10,501, 8,266 and 26,751 policies. Those figures are rate changes and affected-policy counts in the regulator's release, not personalized quotes or a promise about the premium on any one home.

The regulator also said many other companies had asked for lower rates or no increase since January 2024. Requests still under review are not approved cuts. Florida's statement also cited a separate company's average South Florida decrease; that is not one of these four approvals. A renewal premium can still change with coverage, insured value, location, risk and discounts even when an insurer's filed rate moves down.

If your policy is with one of the named companies, compare your actual renewal notice with last year's declarations page. Check the deductible, exclusions and insured value before deciding whether a lower premium is a better deal. Ask your insurer or agent which approved filing applies to your policy and when, and get competing quotes with like-for-like coverage. Financialist's mortgage-shopping guide explains another major housing cost, but it does not quote home insurance premiums.

sources.label: Florida Office of Insurance Regulation, September 22 rate-decrease announcement

title: New York Wants to Shut Polymarket Down: What the Lawsuit Actually Says
description: New York sued Polymarket, alleging unlicensed gambling and seeking a shutdown, penalties and restitution. The allegations are contested, not a court ruling or an approved refund.
author: James Park
body: New York has sued Polymarket US, asking a court to stop what the state calls an unlicensed gambling operation. The September 24 complaint also seeks penalties, forfeiture of alleged illegal gains and restitution for harmed users. A lawsuit is not a judgment. No restitution program or claim form for Polymarket users has been announced in the state release.

The New York attorney general says Polymarket's prediction markets let people stake money on uncertain outcomes, including sports events. The state argues this amounts to gambling that requires a New York license and says the platform is available to users aged 18 to 20 despite a 21-year minimum for mobile sports betting. Those are the state's allegations, not facts a court has resolved.

Prediction-market operators have argued that certain event contracts fall under federal derivatives oversight instead of state gambling rules. The CFTC has separately sued New York over a state prediction-market enforcement dispute involving another operator, so the legal boundary is contested. That federal suit does not itself decide Polymarket's case. Users should not assume a platform is either lawful or unlawful nationwide from this New York filing alone.

New Yorkers considering any event contract should check what entity offers it, their state's applicable rules, the risk of losing the stake, and whether the offer is an investment product or a wager. Anyone claiming an immediate Polymarket restitution payout based on this filing is getting ahead of the court case. The attorney general's release links the official complaint and its misconduct-reporting process; use that source rather than an unsolicited refund message.

sources.label: New York Attorney General September 24 Polymarket lawsuit announcement
CFTC April 24 New York prediction-market jurisdiction lawsuit (separate operator/dispute)

title: Colorado Health Premiums Rise 10% for 2027, but Subsidized Bills Tell Another Story
description: Colorado approved an average 10% individual-market premium rise for 2027. State assistance may limit the average net increase for aided shoppers; your bill depends on plan and eligibility.
author: James Park
body: Colorado's insurance regulator has approved an average 10% premium increase in the individual health insurance market for plan year 2027. That is the statewide average before each household's plan choice and financial assistance are applied, not a 10% increase for every person buying coverage.

The Colorado Division of Insurance says its rate review reduced proposed premiums by an estimated $42.1 million across the upcoming plan year. It separately estimates an average $20 monthly net premium increase for financially assisted customers from 2026 to 2027 under Colorado Premium Assistance. Without that support, the regulator estimates the average increase for that group would exceed three times as much, around $69 monthly. These are agency estimates for a group, not household price quotes.

The regulator reports an average 14% increase for the small-group market, which serves participating employers, and shows individual-market increases ranging from 5.9% to 15.5% across its nine rating areas. A consumer may see a different change based on location, age, insurer, plan and subsidy. An increase in the sticker price and an increase after aid are different measures.

Colorado says marketplace open enrollment begins November 1, 2026, and plans from a new individual-market insurer, Colorado Access, will be offered. Before renewing, compare the 2027 premium after actual aid, deductible, provider network and prescription coverage, not only a statewide rate headline. Financialist's Maryland ACA report covers a different state's filings; those figures should not be applied to Colorado.

sources.label: Colorado Division of Insurance September 22 approved-rate announcement

title: Amazon Prime Refunds Expand to $200; More Checks Start October 1
description: A revised FTC-Amazon order raises the Prime refund cap to $200 and adds automatic payments starting October 1, 2026. Who may be included and how to avoid refund scams.
author: David Chen
body: More former and current Prime customers may receive refunds without filing a new claim beginning October 1 under a revised federal court order. The FTC says the maximum total payment rises from $51 to $200 and Amazon must distribute future payments automatically. A $200 cap is not a promise of a $200 check to every subscriber.

The revision expands automatic payments to people who used between 11 and 20 Prime benefits in a one-year period after enrollment; those people were outside the earlier phases. Amazon will make payments electronically through Venmo or PayPal or mail checks, the FTC says. Customers should not need to respond to a new claim notice or complete additional forms to receive these future payments.

There may also be a later top-up for people who already received and accepted a settlement refund. If accepted payments do not reach the required threshold by February 2027, the FTC says those consumers could get up to $149 more, bringing their total up to $200; that supplemental round would start by April 2027. The condition matters: it is not an unconditional additional payment today.

The FTC says it is not contacting consumers about these Amazon refunds and warns that anyone claiming to be the agency and asking for payment is likely a scam. Amazon will not ask customers to pay a fee to receive a refund. Check the September 17 FTC release for the revised terms. Its separate refund-program FAQ still described an older $51 cap when checked September 27, so the newer court-order announcement controls this update; readers should watch for that older FAQ to be revised.

sources.label: FTC September 17 revised Prime refund order announcement
FTC Amazon refund-program FAQ (older cap shown September 27)

internal_links.label: Protect your credit reports from fraud

title: Bought a Generic Drug Years Ago? Check This $96 Million Settlement Before March 8
description: A multistate generic-drug settlement has a March 8, 2027 claim deadline. Check the covered drugs, 2009-2019 purchase window and eligibility before filing.
author: James Park
body: People who bought certain generic prescription drugs from May 2009 through December 2019 may be eligible for compensation from multistate antitrust settlements. The claim deadline is March 8, 2027, according to the New York attorney general. Coverage depends on the particular drug, purchase period and the official settlement rules; buying any generic medicine is not enough.

New York and Connecticut attorneys general describe settlements totaling approximately $96 million with several drug manufacturers. Connecticut says a federal court granted preliminary approval to a plan for distributing consumer funds. Preliminary approval and an open claims window do not mean a particular person will receive a specific payment. The individual amount depends on valid claims and the settlement process.

To check eligibility, use the official settlement website linked from a state attorney general's announcement and review the covered-drug list and instructions. New York's announcement directs consumers to AGGenericDrugs.com. Do not enter prescription or payment information into a lookalike site reached through an unsolicited message. The state notices also give a telephone contact for questions.

The purchase window is long enough that receipts may be hard to find. Read the administrator's actual proof requirements before assuming a claim is impossible or guaranteed. A pharmacist's statement, insurance record or old receipt may help reconstruct a purchase, but the administrator decides whether evidence satisfies the settlement terms. This claim is separate from disputing a current medical bill; Financialist's medical-debt guide explains that other process.

sources.label: New York Attorney General consumer claim announcement
Connecticut Attorney General preliminary-approval and purchase-window notice

title: Paid a Surprise Maryland Hospital Fee? Some UMMS Patients Are Getting Refunds
description: A Maryland settlement will return $2.25 million in outpatient facility fees to eligible UMMS patients. Who qualifies, when checks are expected and what the state says.
author: David Chen
body: Some Maryland patients who paid out of pocket for outpatient facility fees at University of Maryland Medical System clinics may receive checks under a $2.25 million restitution agreement announced by the state attorney general. The eligible services were provided before July 1, 2021, and refunds are expected over the next six months. Patients do not have to guess from the size of a past hospital bill whether they qualify.

The agreement concerns fees charged by certain hospital clinics when a patient could have received the same clinic service at a non-hospital facility owned or operated by a UMMS affiliate without the facility fee. Maryland's Consumer Protection Division alleged patients were not adequately told they would be charged. UMMS denied that the notice was inadequate but agreed to pay $2,251,781.52 in restitution. This is a settlement, not a finding that every UMMS outpatient fee was unlawful.

The state says eligible patients should expect a refund check from UMMS during the next six months. Its announcement does not provide an individual refund amount, a claims form or a complete list of covered clinics. Do not pay someone to 'unlock' a check. Patients with questions can use the phone number in the attorney general's original announcement; verify it there rather than relying on an unsolicited call or message.

A facility fee is separate from what a clinician may charge for a visit. If a bill seems wrong, ask for an itemized bill and the facility's written explanation. Financialist's medical-debt guide covers reviewing bills and assistance before paying, but it cannot determine eligibility for this particular restitution program.

sources.label: Maryland Attorney General September 25 UMMS facility-fee settlement

title: FTC weighs new duties for platforms carrying impersonation ads
description: Agency seeks evidence about ad tools and impersonation scams. No new platform rule has taken effect.
author: David Chen
body: The Federal Trade Commission is asking whether online platforms should face new obligations when their advertising tools help spread ads that impersonate businesses or government agencies. It has opened an advance notice of proposed rulemaking, not adopted a new rule.

The agency's September 24 notice focuses on ad-optimization services offered by social networks, search engines and digital marketplaces. It seeks evidence about how those tools select audiences and shape the delivery of ads, what platforms do to vet advertisers, and whether changes to the existing Impersonation Rule or a separate rule are warranted. Measures under consideration include advertiser screening, monitoring, removing confirmed scam ads and action against offending advertisers.

The FTC says consumers filed more than one million imposter-scam reports in 2025 and reported nearly $3.5 billion in losses. Those are reported losses, not an estimate of all fraud. The agency also says nearly 30% of consumers who reported losing money to scammers in 2025 said the first contact was on social media. Neither figure by itself proves a platform caused a particular loss.

The public comment deadline will be 60 days after the notice appears in the Federal Register. That publication date, rather than September 24, sets the clock. No new platform duty takes effect from this notice alone.

For people searching online for help with a bill or debt, the distinction between an official service and an ad that copies its name matters. Before providing account information or paying a supposed relief provider, navigate independently to the agency or provider's official site. Financialist's state-by-state debt help guide is a separate starting point for understanding state-specific debt rules; it is not a substitute for checking an offer's identity.

sources.label: FTC September 24 announcement on impersonation-ad rulemaking

title: September 28 tax deadline approaches for eligible San Carlos Apache Tribe disaster area taxpayers
description: Eligible taxpayers in the San Carlos Apache Tribe disaster area have a September 28 deadline for many postponed filings and payments.
author: James Park
body: Taxpayers covered by IRS disaster relief for severe storms and flooding in the San Carlos Apache Tribe area face a September 28 deadline for many postponed federal tax filings and payments. The relief is limited to eligible affected taxpayers; it is not a nationwide extension.

According to the IRS, qualifying individuals who live in the covered area and businesses whose principal place of business is there can use the postponement. Others whose records needed to meet a deadline are in the covered area can also qualify. The IRS lists additional categories, including eligible relief workers. The postponed window generally covers specified deadlines originally falling on or after October 10, 2025, and before September 28, 2026.

Estimated income tax payments that originally fell in that window are postponed through September 28. The IRS says affected taxpayers will not be penalized for failing to pay those installments if they pay by that date. Not every form or deposit is covered: the agency lists exceptions for certain information returns and employment and excise tax deposits. Anyone relying on the relief should check the complete IRS notice against their own filing obligation.

Eligible taxpayers in the federally declared disaster area may also choose whether to claim qualifying uncovered casualty losses for the disaster year or the prior year. The IRS says individual taxpayers have until October 15, 2026, to make that election. A casualty-loss claim involves separate eligibility and documentation rules; the postponed filing deadline does not automatically establish a deductible loss.

Financialist's Arizona debt-help guide covers a different topic, state debt rules, for readers managing obligations after the storm. It does not explain eligibility for federal disaster tax relief; use the IRS notice for that decision.

sources.label: IRS disaster tax-relief notice for San Carlos Apache Tribe area

title: Hawaii joins proposed Credit Acceptance auto-loan settlement with debt relief
description: Proposed multistate settlement offers potential cash restitution and debt relief for eligible Credit Acceptance borrowers.
author: James Park
body: Hawaii has joined a proposed multistate settlement with auto lender Credit Acceptance Corporation over allegations involving unaffordable loans and add-on products. The consent judgment still needs court approval in participating states, so the proposed relief should not be described as money already paid to every borrower.

In a September 23 announcement, Hawaii's Office of Consumer Protection said the nationwide settlement could provide up to $60 million in cash restitution and up to $634 million in debt forgiveness, with up to $15 million going to settling attorneys general. Those are nationwide maximums or prospective amounts, not a per-person payout. Hawaii expects eligible borrowers in the state to receive nearly $115,000 in direct payments in total and nearly $830,000 in debt relief in total, some of which the office says may already have been provided.

The state says investigators alleged that Credit Acceptance originated some loans it knew or should have known borrowers could not afford. They also alleged that dealers in its network added vehicle service contracts and guaranteed asset protection products without consumers understanding the purchase or believing the products were required to finance the car. These are allegations resolved by the proposed settlement, not findings in this article.

If approved, the judgment would require new disclosures, monitoring of add-on sales and a process to cancel certain products more easily. For qualifying risky loans made beginning December 2025 that fail quickly, the settlement describes a five-year program beginning November 2, 2026, under which qualifying borrowers would get 95% debt relief and would not face collection suits on those loans. Not every Credit Acceptance borrower qualifies.

The Hawaii office says Credit Acceptance must contact consumers entitled to certain types of relief. Borrowers should verify their eligibility through official channels and not assume that an unsolicited message requesting an upfront fee is legitimate. Financialist's Hawaii debt guide offers background on state debt rules, separate from the settlement's eligibility terms.

sources.label: Hawaii Office of Consumer Protection September 23 announcement

title: States reach $2.3 million Labcorp settlement over debt collector's data breach
description: Forty-four states reached an agreement with Labcorp over patient data held by a medical debt collector.
author: David Chen
body: A coalition of 44 state attorneys general has reached an approximately $2.3 million settlement with Labcorp over a 2019 data breach at a medical debt collector that handled Labcorp patient information. The agreement focuses on how the laboratory company oversees vendors holding sensitive patient data; the state announcement does not describe this $2.3 million as a consumer refund fund.

Delaware Attorney General Kathy Jennings announced the settlement September 24. The debt collector was Retrieval-Masters Creditors Bureau, doing business as American Medical Collection Agency, or AMCA. The breach potentially exposed information about more than 27.5 million people nationwide, including 10.2 million Labcorp patients, according to the Delaware announcement. "Potentially exposed" does not mean every person's data was misused.

Under the agreement described by Delaware, Labcorp will strengthen its vendor risk program, maintain an incident-response process for vendor security events, limit sharing of data where appropriate, and impose additional security standards and assessment requirements on debt-collection vendors. A third-party assessor will review its information-security program with a focus on vendor risk management. Labcorp's payment to the states is $2,287,455, including $30,135 to Delaware.

The state distinguishes this multistate agreement from a separate $35 million class-action settlement related to the breach. Consumers should not confuse the two or infer a personal payment from the states' agreement. The Delaware announcement does not set out a claims process for individuals under this state settlement.

Medical bills can reach a collector even when the original provider's name is more familiar to the patient. Anyone contacted about an old medical balance can ask for written details and check the debt independently before providing financial information. Financialist's state debt guides cover general collection rules by location; they do not determine whether someone was affected by this breach.

sources.label: Delaware Department of Justice September 24 announcement

title: Nano Banc deposits transfer to Sunwest after California closure
description: What customers can use this weekend and when the only branch reopens.
author: James Park
body: Nano Banc customers can continue using checks, ATMs and debit cards this weekend after California regulators closed the Irvine bank on Friday. The FDIC says Sunwest Bank of Sandy, Utah has agreed to assume substantially all Nano Banc deposits and buy some of its assets. Customers automatically become Sunwest depositors; the deposits Sunwest assumes remain FDIC-insured.

The FDIC says Nano Banc's only branch is scheduled to reopen Monday, September 28, under Sunwest during normal business hours. Checks written on Nano Banc accounts will continue to be processed, and loan customers should keep making their payments as usual. The agency says customers have immediate access to their deposits; they do not have to open a new account to make their assumed deposits available.

Nano Banc reported $686 million in deposits and $736 million in total assets as of June 30, according to the FDIC. Sunwest is buying approximately $476 million of assets; the FDIC will retain the rest for later disposition. The agency's preliminary estimate of the cost to the Deposit Insurance Fund is about $114 million. That is an estimated fund cost, not an amount charged to Nano Banc depositors; the estimate could change when assets are sold.

A bank closure often brings phishing attempts. Rather than follow a text claiming an urgent account migration, customers can use the FDIC's original notice for its official contact information and the bank's verified channels. FDIC deposit insurance coverage depends on account ownership and institution, not just an account balance. Financialist's bank-fees guide covers a different issue, overdraft rules, for people reviewing banking costs.

sources.label: FDIC September 25 Nano Banc closure notice

title: Maryland approves 2027 ACA rates: 14.6% average increase before subsidies
description: Regulator figures show why a market average and a household bill differ.
author: David Chen
body: Maryland approved 2027 health insurance premium rates on Friday. The state insurance regulator says unsubsidized individual Affordable Care Act plan premiums will rise 14.6% on average. That is a statewide market average, not a prediction of what every Maryland household will pay: a plan's price, the member's age and any subsidy can change the bill.

Maryland's published example makes the variation concrete. For a 40-year-old in the Baltimore metro area looking at the lowest-cost off-exchange silver plans, the listed monthly unsubsidized change ranges from $9 for an Optimum Choice HMO (from $342 to $350, as rounded in the regulator table) to $89 for a CareFirst PPO (from $585 to $674). These are sample plan figures, not statewide averages or quotes for a specific reader. An off-exchange example also does not show financial assistance available through Maryland Health Connection.

The Maryland Insurance Administration says roughly 70% of Maryland Health Connection users and 55% of the overall individual market receive a premium subsidy. The state has its own assistance program for eligible residents with household incomes below 400% of the federal poverty level. Those eligible for assistance may see a different net premium change from the 14.6% unsubsidized figure. The regulator says individual market enrollment stands at about 274,000, down from 294,000 last year.

Small-group premiums for employers with no more than 50 full-time employees are approved to rise 10.2% on average. That is below carriers' 13.1% requested increase. The regulator reports rising hospital and prescription costs as main drivers and puts the separate individual dental-market average increase at 3.0%.

Consumers should read their renewal notice and compare actual 2027 plans and assistance eligibility when enrollment opens. A health premium is not the same as a medical bill: Financialist's medical-debt guide explains ways to check and contest charges after care, not how ACA subsidies are calculated.

sources.label: Maryland Insurance Administration September 25 rate approval

title: IRS adds account notices and tax records to free mobile app
description: Official app adds selected account features; watch for tax-account lookalikes.
author: James Park
body: The IRS launched a renamed mobile app Friday, extending the older IRS2Go service with access to some Individual Online Account features. The agency says taxpayers can now use the free IRS app to view available balances, selected notices and tax transcripts, check refund or amended-return status and review payment activity. An account-specific feature may require secure sign-in; an app download by itself does not display private records.

Existing IRS2Go users do not need to download a separate replacement. The agency says normal app updates will deliver the new version for users with automatic updates enabled. The app is available in the Apple App Store and Google Play, and IRS.gov provides verified links. The IRS says the app does not replace the full website or its Business Tax Account and Tax Pro Account services. This first release extends selected individual features only.

For taxpayers with an approaching filing or payment deadline, the balance and payment-history features could be useful, but the app does not change the legal due date or automatically pay a balance. The IRS also says users may access an Identity Protection PIN through the app. Readers should not take a text message or search ad offering tax-account access as proof that an app is official: the IRS warns it will not request sensitive financial information through an unsolicited text, email or pop-up.

The September 28 disaster tax deadline for eligible San Carlos Apache Tribe-area taxpayers remains a separate IRS relief rule. Financialist's existing deadline report explains who is covered; the new app neither extends that window nor determines eligibility.

sources.label: IRS September 25 app launch announcement

title: Michigan attorney general challenges UPPCO electric rate hike
description: A proposed 15.6% residential increase is not approved; state advocates a smaller increase.
author: James Park
body: Michigan's attorney general is asking regulators to cut a proposed Upper Peninsula Power Company electric rate hike. UPPCO seeks an additional $17.3 million in annual revenue, which the attorney general says would mean a 15.6% average increase for residential customers. Neither the company request nor the attorney general's counterproposal is an approved new customer rate.

In testimony filed jointly with the Citizens Utility Board of Michigan, Attorney General Dana Nessel argued Friday that any increase should be no more than $9.9 million, a cut of roughly 42% from the request. The attorney general also opposed UPPCO's requested return on equity increase from 9.86% to 10.55%, proposing instead 9.47%. These percentages concern the utility's allowed return, not the rate printed on a household bill.

Another household-level dispute is the residential fixed monthly charge. Nessel said the proposed $15 charge should be reduced to $10.87. A fixed charge applies even when a household uses less electricity, so its size can matter to customers who conserve power. The attorney general also objected to a proposed storm-restoration expense tracker that, she says, could lead to adjustments between the normal public rate cases. The Michigan Public Service Commission will decide the case.

UPPCO serves approximately 53,000 Upper Peninsula customers, according to the attorney general's office. A 15.6% average residential increase is not a quote for a particular home: usage, rate design and whatever the commission ultimately approves will determine that amount. Financialist's money-rights hub addresses other household expenses, including bank fees and medical bills; it does not calculate UPPCO electric charges. Customers should use their utility's rate documents and the commission's final order for bill-specific figures.

sources.label: Michigan Attorney General September 25 UPPCO testimony

title: Michigan sues generator sellers over customer deposits
description: State alleges customers paid deposits but did not receive generators or refunds.
author: David Chen
body: Michigan's attorney general filed a consumer-protection lawsuit seeking refunds for customers who allegedly paid deposits for home generators they never received. The case names Triple Circle, Double Circle, Goodrich Enterprise and Brad Scott, who, according to the state, were associated with two former Generator Supercenter franchise locations. The allegations have not been decided by a court, and a lawsuit is not a restitution payment.

The state says the franchises continued accepting thousands of dollars in deposits even as they were nearing closure. Its complaint alleges some customers never received generators or refunds, including customers who cancelled orders. The filing also alleges that business revenue, including consumer deposits, was used for personal purchases. Michigan filed the case in Kent County Circuit Court on September 8 and announced Friday that the defendants had been served this week.

According to the attorney general's account, the two franchise businesses were formed under agreements in late 2020 and the franchisor terminated those agreements in April 2024. The state seeks restitution and monetary damages for affected customers, an injunction and civil fines. It has not announced a claims deadline or an approved distribution amount.

Michigan residents who believe they are affected can contact the attorney general's Consumer Protection Team through the state website rather than pay a third party promising access to a refund. Documents such as the contract, deposit receipt, cancellation request and correspondence may help establish an individual claim. Financialist's Michigan debt guide is about collection rules, not this lawsuit, but can help readers facing separate bills while a disputed deposit remains unpaid.

sources.label: Michigan Attorney General September 25 lawsuit announcement

title: New York warns of storm price gouging: what to document
description: State alert explains the emergency-pricing standard and what a useful complaint records.
author: David Chen
body: New York's attorney general issued a consumer alert Saturday as a severe coastal storm was expected to bring heavy rain, wind and possible flooding to New York City, the Hudson Valley and Long Island. The warning concerns the price of essential goods and services during an emergency, not every price increase after a storm.

The attorney general's office says New York law bars businesses from taking unfair advantage by charging an unconscionably excessive price for goods or services vital to health, safety or welfare during an emergency. The state says the law covers New York vendors, including those selling online. Whether a particular charge breaks the law depends on its circumstances; the alert does not set a flat percentage threshold or make every expensive hotel room, generator or repair job a violation.

For a report, the office asks consumers to note the specific price increase, date and location. Save a receipt and take a photo of an advertised price where possible. A before-and-after price comparison can help an investigator understand the complaint, though the office decides whether to investigate and whether the legal standard is met. New Yorkers can submit a complaint through the attorney general's official website or call the number in its alert.

The office says violations may carry penalties of up to $25,000 per violation. That is a potential civil penalty on a business, not a consumer refund amount or a guarantee that a complaint will produce payment. Anyone hiring a storm-repair contractor should also get the full price and work scope in writing before paying a deposit. Financialist's New York debt guide explains separate rules for collecting a bill; it is not a guide to storm price-gouging complaints.

sources.label: New York Attorney General September 26 consumer alert
